sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: FLAG immunostaining: reduced surface expression for M1/M5 variants vs. WT (L1). Fusogenic activity with C2C12 myoblasts: retained at residual level for M1/M5 (L2). Reduction attributed to M1/M5 disease mutations, not the FLAG tag position.
sites.rationale: MYMK has exactly one extracellular terminus: the N-terminus (residues 1–3, MGT), since the C-terminus (residues 196–221) is intracellular per the topology landmarks. The topology-derived rule therefore places the FLAG tag as an N-terminal prepend (insert_after_residue=0, residue_after=M). FLAG immunostaining without permeabilization in L1 confirms the tag is extracellularly accessible, consistent with this placement. No residue number is stated in either clip, so the position is topology-derived, not validated. Full-length FLAG-tagged human MYMK (M1 and M5 variant) constructs expressed in fibroblasts; FLAG antibody immunostaining without permeabilization confirmed extracellular accessibility of the tag, establishing it is on the extracellular face.

sources.claim: We found, however, that immunostaining with a FLAG antibody revealed a low percentage of M1 and M5 transfected protein at the membrane compared to WT.

literature_notes: L1 and L2 both describe the same FLAG-tagged MYMK constructs from PMC5504296; neither names the insertion residue. MYMK has only one extracellular terminus (N-term, residues 1–3), making the topology-derived N-terminal prepend the only defensible placement. The extracellular loops (EC1: 50–64, EC2: 110–116, EC3: 172–177) are possible alternative positions, but the ledger provides no loop-specific insertion evidence and the topology-derived rule applies only to the sole extracellular terminus. The C-terminus (196–221) is intracellular and was not considered for a surface tag. No ledger line names a specific residue or loop for the FLAG insertion, and no line reports an insertion that abrogates function at a named position.
